messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: platform support decisions
parts:
Here's the story about C++ standards:

C++98: 1998 ISO C++ Standard
C++03: 2003 ISO C++ Technical Corrigendum
C++11: 2011 ISO C++ Standard

I think C++98 is out of date in the sense that C++03 is
the default mode in both g++ and clang++.

I think C++11 is premature in that gtest doesn't support
it yet, nor do Eigen or Boost reliably.

So with the wisdom of Solomon and Goldilocks, I think
we should target C++03 and only C++03 for now.

For the Mac, I think we can safely restrict ourselves to the
latest Xcode versions of g++ and clang++ with their own default
libs:

Xcode 4.5.2 g++ 4.2.1, {O=0, O=3}, C++03
Xcode 4.5.2 clang++ 3.1, {O=0, O=3}, C++03

All four of these tests with the current repository version.

I added a new section at the top of the TestUnitStats listing
"supported" platforms. The idea of "support" is that we won't
release unless all tests pass on these platforms.

I added this as the list of "supported" platforms on the Wiki for
the Mac.

Could someone do the same for Windows and Linux and make sure
the current tests pass?

If we can do this, I think we should roll out Stan 1.0.4 this weekend
or early next week.

- Bob

On Friday, December 14, 2012 3:27:44 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Here's the story about C++ standards:

    C++98:  1998 ISO C++ Standard
    C++03:  2003 ISO C++ Technical Corrigendum
    C++11:  2011 ISO C++ Standard

I think C++98 is out of date in the sense that C++03 is
the default mode in both g++ and clang++.

Almost, see

http://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Standards.html

under the C++ section. "The default, if no C++ language dialect options are given, is -std=gnu++98." so we would need to specify -std=c++03 explicitly, which is probably a good idea.

Ben

I think we should clarify that g++ 4.2.1 on Xcode is really llvm-g++ 4.2.1. Pure g++ is generally fine on Linux, so it is presumably OK on Mac. But aside from Daniel maybe testing with pure g++ 4.6, I don't think we know much about pure g++ on a Mac (not that the average user would be downloading it).

Ben
